what_this_is: Executable falsifications. Each arm names a gate, a mutation to a tracked file, and the command that must go RED. `scripts/check_gate_registry.py --demonstrate` applies the mutation to the real tree, runs the real gate, requires a non-zero exit AND the recorded diagnostic, then restores the file from git. A demonstration in this repo is a thing that RUNS, not a sentence in a header that was true once.
rules: An arm refuses to run if its target file is already dirty; it restores from git and will not clobber an edit.
An arm that finds the UNMUTATED gate already red is a FAILURE, not a pass: a red arm on a red tree proves nothing.
A mutation whose pattern does not match is a FAILURE, not a skip. That silent no-op is instance 4 (four perturbation batteries, vacuous because a failed substitution never aborted).
expect_contains pins WHY it went red. A gate that exits non-zero for an unrelated reason has not been demonstrated.

clean-cli::help_truth.arm: the code a claim cites moves out from under its citation
clean-cli::help_truth.why: MEASURED 2026-09-01. A file:line citation alone is nearly worthless: any edit ABOVE the line shifts the target silently, so the citation keeps resolving while pointing somewhere else. Each claim therefore carries an `anchor` substring that must still appear on the cited line. This arm renames the printed string the claim was verified against, which is exactly the shape of a real refactor, and the gate refuses rather than continuing to cite a line that no longer says what it said.

family_gate.arm: A1: a probe's statement edited without a re-mint of pinned Lean's verdicts

family_gate.arm: A2: a comment-only edit is an edit too (the digest pins no normalisation)

family_gate.arm: A3: a hand-flipped Lean verdict (reject -> accept) in the committed sidecar

family_gate.why: The cheapest way to make a false acceptance disappear from the two-way count is to flip Lean's verdict on the row Clean accepts (p_auto_grind_10: pinned Lean's `grind` fails on `gsDouble 2 = 4`). The sidecar stores Lean's messages and the row's #print axioms reading beside the verdict, and --static re-derives every verdict and class from them through lean_verdicts.classify -- so a flip that leaves the stored messages and axioms in place is refused with no Lean on the host, resealed or not (pinned by test_a_hand_flipped_verdict_does_not_re_derive_even_resealed). What --static CANNOT see: the seal is a plain sha256, so a forger who also rewrites the messages and axioms to match and recomputes the seal re-derives cleanly; only `mint_lean_verdicts.py --check`, which asks pinned Lean again (the FULL-mode tactic-lean-verdicts leg), refuses that.

family_gate.arm: A4: one stored Lean message edited (the verdict still re-derives; only the seal can see it)
family_gate.why: An edit that keeps every verdict re-derivable (the message is still an error, so the class stays elab-error) and forgets the seal is caught by the content seal alone: sha256 over canonical JSON of everything but minted_at_utc, seal and lean_world.version_line. It is a check against an edit, not a forger, who can recompute it (see A3).

family_gate.arm: A5: the sidecar claims another Lean world
